items.question: Which selector chooses every element with class="note"?
items.explanation: A dot means class. A hash (#) means id. Classes can be reused on many elements.

items.question: Which selector chooses the single element with id="title"?
items.explanation: The # symbol selects an id. An id must be unique on the page.

items.question: Type the property that changes the color of the text.
items.explanation: color sets the text color. background-color sets the background.
items.hint: It is also the English word for it.

items.question: What is the best way to style many pages with the same rules?
options: An inline style attribute on every tag
items.explanation: An external file lets one set of rules style every page, and you change the design in only one place.

items.question: What color is the text?
items.code: p { color: red; } .note { color: green; }
items.explanation: A class selector (.note) is more specific than an element selector (p), so green wins even though both rules match.

items.question: Type the property that adds space INSIDE the box, between the content and the border.
items.explanation: padding is inside the border. margin is outside it.

items.question: What does margin: 10px 20px; mean?
options: 10px top and bottom, 20px left and right
10px left and right, 20px top and bottom
items.explanation: With two values, the first is top and bottom, and the second is left and right.

items.question: By default (content-box), what is the total width this box takes on screen?
items.explanation: The width only covers the content. Total = 300 + padding (20 + 20) + border (2 + 2) = 344px. The rule box-sizing: border-box makes width include them.
items.hint: Add the padding and border to the width.

items.question: Type the value that turns a container into a flex container.
items.explanation: display: flex lays the children out in a row and unlocks justify-content, align-items and gap.

items.question: Which property spaces flex items along the main direction (for example centers them in a row)?
items.explanation: justify-content works along the main axis. align-items works across it.

items.question: Type the missing unit so the grid has three equal columns.
items.explanation: 1fr means one share of the free space, so three 1fr columns are equal.

items.question: Write a media query that makes h1 use font-size: 1.6rem when the screen is 600px wide or less.
items.explanation: A media query applies its rules only when the condition is true. max-width: 600px matches screens that are 600px wide or smaller.
